title: Install or recover Weaver
summary: Install the Weaver CLI and provider and save its Annals reader configuration through the product command without authoring a document.
use_when: Install the Weaver CLI and provider and save its Annals reader configuration through the product command without authoring a document.
do_not_use_when: Publication, email, automatic scheduling, source mutation, factual certification, or restoration of the retired Weaver workflow is wanted.
outcome: Install the Weaver CLI and provider and save its Annals reader configuration through the product command without authoring a document.
effects: Install selects immutable program and provider bytes, initializes supported Weaver SQLite state and stores reading configuration under ordinary admission and the runner lock. It creates and releases no maintenance hold. It creates no narrative, model job, email, or schedule.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Weaver/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity.
authority: Weaver owns authored Markdown, exact authoring requests, one pending mailbox reply per document, observed execution outcomes, reading configuration, and deployment admission.

Annals owns accepted source documents. Krisis owns decision identification. Nucleus owns execution, authentication, and its retained history. The agent owns editorial interpretation under the user direction.
success: Installed program/provider selection and product initialization/configuration establish completed setup. Separately acquired maintenance holds keep their own completion rules. Installation does not establish operational readiness.
failure_and_recovery: Resume an uncertain invocation using the identical saved request and job ID. Terminal jobs receive no automatic replacement. Saved documents survive later runtime failure. Deployment retains completed effects and performs no automatic product recovery. Preserve separately acquired holds.
privacy: Requests, documents, and pending tool replies are private. Nucleus may retain full source reads. Weaver clears acknowledged replies and keeps documents and invocation records without automatic pruning.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID in its private journal. Arguments, output, outcomes, and internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
does_not_authorize: Source mutation, remote disclosure, publication, email, state deletion, automatic retry, or effects outside the user-approved endpoint.

consumers.statement: The current local user and authorized Cell agents follow this procedure within the agreed change or maintenance endpoint.

preconditions.statement: Authorized installation or configuration, compatible Annals and Nucleus releases, an existing decisions library, and attributable product-owned selectors. First installation requires annals_config settings.

Prompt preparation requires initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.weaver selection. The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3; callers accept an absolute CELL_BAZAAR_DATABASE override. Reads fail without creating state or using embedded fallback text.

New authoring requires initialized Bazaar state and complete cell.prompts.weaver selection. Import the reviewed migration seed before deployment and preserve its historical selection/text versions; deployment does not supply missing contents.

inputs.statement: Submit committed source through ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy weaver from the Cell root. CI and Telete are the sole deployment route. --settings ABSOLUTE_JSON supplies private JSON whose weaver object contains annals_config, an absolute existing decisions-library config; Telete freezes the values for the job. Init also accepts an absolute annals_binary. Hold and release take exact owner IDs.

outputs.statement: The product command selects programs and provider, saves the Annals reader configuration and initializes supported state under ordinary admission and the runner lock. It creates and releases no maintenance hold.

data_semantics.statement: Installation success means local program/provider selection and configuration. It performs no artifact-integrity, state-integrity, or dependency-readiness checks and creates no narrative or email.

identity_and_units.statement: Source commit, executor request ID and retained manager job identities select delivery. Exact run IDs own separately requested maintenance holds. These are separate from authoring document and job identities.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installer inspection describes release metadata. Doctor and other diagnostics remain separate; installation and catalog presence do not establish live readiness.
No end-to-end delivery, source-read or authoring completion latency is promised.

access.statement: Use the current-user CLI, registered Semantics reader, installed manager, and maintained Telete deployment manager. Keep configuration, sources, and runtime records private.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The executor runs the declared product command. Weaver selects program and provider files and writes reading configuration and state under ordinary admission and the runner lock. Deployment creates no hold, drains no authoring job and invokes no readiness probe. Failed instructions retain completed effects without automatic retry, rollback or product recovery.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Weaver/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity.

operational_limits.statement: Readiness probes create no model jobs or synthetic narratives. The procedure preserves private state, owned holds, exact authoring recovery and source authority.
No throughput, retention horizon, future model availability, or automatic authoring retry objective is declared.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Preserve existing public command routes, schema 1, historical exact requests, immutable tool identities and matched program/provider selection. The owned features declare their detailed compatibility rules.
No future compatibility lifetime or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: The installed CI manager owns serial integration, validation, bounded repair, exact-source deployment and the deterministic outcome email.

Telete validates, prepares signed programs and executes explicitly selected ordered product instructions. It retains source and request correlation and process outcomes. Products own setup, state, maintenance and recovery.

session_surfaces: Weaver current-user CLI and private configuration
Cell source tree and installed Telete manager
Telete deployment records and product-owned installation evidence
steps: Select the intended committed source and explicit CI deployment products.
Check explicit Annals reading configuration, compatible providers, supported state and complete Bazaar prompt selection.
Prepare private first-installation settings and submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy weaver --settings ABSOLUTE_JSON from the Cell root. Add required dependency products explicitly.
Let Telete validate, prepare signed programs, and run the declared product command to select program and provider files and write configuration and state under ordinary admission.
Inspect release metadata and register command inventory. Use doctor separately when live diagnostics are needed.
For attended maintenance, own a hold, settle exact work, prove drain, verify and release only that hold.
Inspect interrupted execution evidence and current product state. Complete any authorized product recovery separately, then acknowledge executor admission after the original execution has stopped.
checkpoints: First installation identifies an existing identity-bound Annals decisions config and only supported settings.
The caller selects required product and dependency updates explicitly; the executor does not infer compatibility or add products.
Deployment runs no model job, narrative, source-read probe or readiness diagnostic.
The installed overview, focused feature pages and resolve closure describe the matched release.
The retained delivery outcome establishes instruction completion. Application readiness and release of separately acquired maintenance holds require their own evidence.
adaptation: Reuse stored reading configuration on later deployments unless a deliberate setting changes it.
Use ordinary doctor admission while unheld; while held require the deployment ID to match Weaver's sole hold.
Settle retained assignments with exact resume; cancel only a named Nucleus job the authorized operation intends to abandon.
Retain completed deployment effects and current application state after failure. Use explicit product interfaces for recovery and a new executor request ID for an authorized new attempt.
stop_when: State is unsupported or missing outside an authorized initialization.
A required setup interface is unavailable, ordinary admission is held, or an explicit maintenance operation cannot prove drain.
A selector is foreign, a declared instruction fails, or the plan exceeds the authorized scope.
An interrupted instruction has unknown effects; inspect current product state before any authorized new attempt.
